originalTitle: Death row inmates desperate to escape execution in Saudi Arabia call the BBC
title: People from Ethiopia Need Kind Hearts
content:
Hello, Friends! Welcome to Our African News!

Hello, my wonderful friends! I am your special news reporter, and I bring you important stories from our amazing continent, Africa, and sometimes about our friends who live far away. Today, we have a story that needs our kind hearts and our listening ears. It is about some people from a country called Ethiopia. Ethiopia is a beautiful country right here in Africa. It is a place with lots of history, yummy food, and friendly people, just like you and me.

Where is Ethiopia?

Did you know that Africa is a very, very big continent? It has many countries, and Ethiopia is one of them! It’s in the eastern part of Africa. If you look at a map of Africa, you will see it. Imagine a big animal, and Ethiopia is one of its spots! Many people live there. They have schools, homes, and playgrounds, just like where you live. They have families and friends too.

Going to a Faraway Land

Sometimes, grown-ups travel very far away from their homes. They might go to another country to find work. They want to earn money to send back to their families. This money helps buy food, clothes, and send children to school. It is a big adventure for them to travel so far. Our friends from Ethiopia also traveled to a country called Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia is a country far, far away from Africa. You would need to fly in an airplane for many hours to get there!

A Big Problem in Saudi Arabia

Sadly, some of our friends from Ethiopia who went to Saudi Arabia are now in a very big problem. They are very, very sad. They are worried. They miss their homes and their families so much. They are in a place where they are not free to come back home. This makes their families here in Ethiopia very sad too. Imagine missing your mommy or daddy for a very, very long time. That’s how sad they are.

What Does "Big Problem" Mean?

Our friends are facing a very big punishment in Saudi Arabia. This punishment means they might not ever be able to come home to their families in Ethiopia. It's the biggest punishment someone can get in that country. It makes them feel very scared and alone. They feel like they are stuck. They want to go home more than anything in the world. They want to hug their children and see their parents again. Did you know that it's important to follow rules in every country? Sometimes, people make mistakes or get into trouble, even if they didn't mean to. These people from Ethiopia are now asking for someone to help them. They want someone to listen to their story.

Calling for Help!

When people have a big problem, sometimes they try to tell everyone about it. They want grown-ups to listen and help them. Our friends from Ethiopia who are in Saudi Arabia did something very brave. They called a special news company called the BBC.

Who is the BBC?

Did you know what a news company does? A news company, like the BBC, tells stories to many people. They have reporters, just like me! They listen to people's stories and then share them on TV, on the radio, or on the internet. Many people all over the world listen to the BBC. So, when our friends called the BBC, they hoped that many people would hear their sad stories and maybe, just maybe, someone important could help them.

Why They Are So Sad

Imagine you are very far from your home. You miss your toys, your bed, and your friends. Now imagine you are also very scared that you might not ever get to see your family again. That is how our friends from Ethiopia feel. They are thinking about their children growing up without them. They are thinking about their parents getting old without them there. It is a very heavy sadness in their hearts. They called the BBC because they are desperate. Desperate means they really, really need help now. They are crying out for someone to hear them. Did you know that talking about your feelings can help? Even when you are sad or scared, sharing your story can make you feel a little bit better, and it can also help others understand what you are going through. Our friends are using their voices, even from far away.

Our Hearts Can Help

Even though we are young, our hearts can still help. We can send kind thoughts to our friends in Ethiopia and to those who are far away. We can learn about being kind to everyone, no matter where they come from. We can learn about helping people who are in trouble. When we grow up, we can be the people who make a difference in the world. We can be the people who help those who are sad or scared.

What Happens Next?

Now that the BBC has heard their stories, many grown-ups know about the problem. People in different countries, like Ethiopia and other places, will talk about it. They will try to find a way to help our friends come home. It is like a big puzzle, and many people are trying to find the right pieces to solve it. We hope that with many kind hearts working together, our friends from Ethiopia will get the help they need. We hope they can feel safe again. Did you know that sometimes, people from different countries talk to each other to solve big problems? It's called diplomacy, and it means they try to find fair ways to help everyone. This is what we hope will happen for our friends.

Let's Be Kind

So, remember our friends from Ethiopia who are far away and feeling very sad. Let's remember to be kind to everyone we meet. Let's listen when someone needs help. And let's hope that our friends will soon be able to hug their families again. Thank you for listening with your kind hearts, my wonderful friends! This is your African news reporter, signing off for today. Be kind, be brave!
summary: Some people from Ethiopia are in a very difficult situation far away in Saudi Arabia and are asking for help to come home to their families.
whyMatters: It is important because these are our friends from Africa, and everyone deserves kindness and help when they are in big trouble, especially when they miss their families.

originalTitle: Spain's PM blames traffickers after 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta from Morocco
title: Friends on a Big Journey!
content:
Hello, Super Reporters!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly news reporter for Africa, ready to tell you about some important news from across the sea. We're going to talk about a big journey many people made, and how countries helped them.

A Big Trip to Ceuta

Imagine many, many people, like a whole school full of children and grown-ups, all going on a big trip at once! This is a little like what happened recently. Thousands of people travelled from Morocco to a city called Ceuta. Ceuta is a special place. It's a city that belongs to Spain, but it's very close to Morocco in Africa. It's like a little piece of Spain right next to Morocco! *Did you know?* Ceuta is on the very tip of North Africa, right by the sparkling blue sea! It's a busy place where many boats sail.

Why Did People Travel So Far?

These people, sometimes called "migrants," left their homes in Morocco. They were looking for something new. Maybe they wanted to find better jobs for their parents. Perhaps they hoped for better schools for children, just like you! Or maybe they were looking for a safer place to live and play. When things are hard at home, people sometimes look for a new place to start fresh. *Did you know?* People have been moving to new places for thousands of years! Sometimes it's for food, sometimes for safety, and sometimes to discover new lands.

Who Are These Travelers?

These travelers are just like you and me. They are families, mothers, fathers, and many children. They had hopes and dreams for a better life. It can be a very brave thing to leave your home and travel to a new place. It takes a lot of courage to start somewhere new, especially if you don't know anyone there.

What Are "Traffickers"?

Now, sometimes there are people who are not very kind. They are called "traffickers." These bad people try to trick others. They promise to help people travel to new places. But they ask for money, and they don't always help people safely. Sometimes they put people in danger. The leader of Spain, like a head teacher for the whole country, said these traffickers were part of the problem. It's very important to always travel safely with trusted adults. Never go with someone you don't know, even if they promise you wonderful things.

Helping Hands and Safe Returns

When so many people arrived in Ceuta, it was a big surprise! The grown-ups in charge in Spain and Morocco started to work together. They wanted to make sure everyone was safe. Many of the people who travelled to Ceuta were helped to go back to Morocco. This happened quite quickly, as leaders talked and worked things out. It's like when your friends might get lost in a big park, and everyone helps them find their way back home. Many children who travelled were safely reunited with their families.

Countries Working Together

Spain and Morocco are neighbours. Even though they had a tricky situation, they worked together. Working together is like when you and your friends work together on a school project. It helps everyone! Leaders from both countries talked about how to help people and make sure everyone stayed safe. They want to make sure such a big trip happens in a safe and planned way, not all at once and dangerously. *Did you know?* Spain and Morocco have known each other for a very, very long time! They share history, food, and even some words in their languages.

A Special Rule for Travel

Sometimes, countries have special rules about how people can travel between them. It's usually easy for people in many European countries to visit each other. This makes holidays and visiting family very simple! But sometimes, if too many people travel suddenly, a country might pause these easy rules for a little while. This happened with Italy, another country far away. Italy made it a bit harder for people to travel easily between their country and Spain for a short time. This was to help everyone understand what was happening and to keep things calm. It's like when there are too many children on the playground at once, and a teacher might say, "Let's take a little break," to make sure everyone is safe and happy.

What Can We Learn?

This news reminds us of a few important things. Firstly, many people in the world are looking for a better life. They are brave and have hopes for the future. Secondly, it's super important to be safe when travelling. Always be with trusted adults and never with strangers. And finally, countries and people can work together, even when things are difficult. Helping each other makes the world a kinder and safer place for everyone. Let's always remember to be kind and understand people who are on a big journey.
summary: Many people, including kids, travelled from Morocco to the Spanish city of Ceuta looking for a better life, and countries worked together to help them safely.
whyMatters: This is important because it teaches us about why people move, the dangers of bad people called traffickers, and how countries can work together to help everyone be safe and kind. It shows us that everyone deserves help and understanding.
